overview: Two of the three modes of heat transfer — one moves heat through direct contact, the other through the bulk movement of a fluid.
genZNote: Conduction passes it along. Convection just carries the whole crowd.

aspects.label: Mechanism
aspects.valueA: Heat transfers through direct molecular collisions/vibrations within a material, without bulk movement of matter.
aspects.valueB: Heat transfers via the actual bulk movement of a heated fluid (liquid or gas) from one place to another.

aspects.label: Medium Required
aspects.valueA: Solids (most effective), though it occurs in liquids/gases too.
aspects.valueB: Liquids and gases only — cannot occur in rigid solids.

aspects.label: Everyday Example
aspects.valueA: A metal spoon heating up in hot soup.
aspects.valueB: Water heating from the bottom of a pot and circulating upward.
